report_md:
# Kelly sizing — development report

**Verdict: numeric pass, weak-timing caveat (fails the pre-registered placebo
kill).** The skew-aware fractional-Kelly allocator earns **39.39% CAGR / 57.08%
max DD / 0.97 Sharpe** at 1 bp over 2016-2023, above the published TQQQ bar
(36.72% / 82.29% / 0.82) and still above it at 10 bp (37.61%). It clears the
activity floor with **686 fills across 329 independent fill days**. However,
the real CAGR is at the **88th percentile** of 100 circular-shift placebos,
below the pre-registered 90% threshold. The sizing adds 8.9 pp of CAGR over a
static book at the same average weights, but the timing edge is not as cleanly
distinguishable from a lucky allocation path as the beta or decay families.
Development only; 2024-2026 is untouched.

## Development metrics

| Cost | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe | Sortino | Vol | Exposure | Fills | Turnover |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 bp | 39.39% | 57.08% | 0.97 | 1.37 | 44.5% | 99.9% | 686 | 450x |
| 5 bp | 38.61% | 57.13% | 0.96 | 1.35 | 44.5% | 99.9% | 690 | 438x |
| 10 bp | 37.61% | 57.19% | 0.94 | 1.33 | 44.5% | 99.9% | 688 | 422x |

Average weights are 14.8% QQQ, 64.9% TQQQ, 20.3% BIL. The book is aggressive:
it holds TQQQ about two-thirds of the time and uses BIL only when the QQQ Kelly
edge turns negative.

## Subperiods and years

| Window | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 2016-2019 | 34.0% | 45.8% | 0.87 |
| 2020-2021 | 86.9% | 56.9% | 1.13 |
| 2022-2023 | 8.5% | 42.2% | 0.36 |

| Year | Return |
|---|---:|
| 2016 | +23.4% |
| 2017 | +103.9% |
| 2018 | -13.9% |
| 2019 | +38.1% |
| 2020 | +96.2% |
| 2021 | +84.7% |
| 2022 | -39.4% |
| 2023 | +94.2% |

The 2022 drawdown is the weak point: the overlay's rolling mean turns negative
only after the damage, and the QQQ gate moves the book to BIL late. The
2022-2023 subperiod is still positive because 2023 recovers strongly.

## Plateau (pre-registered 8 cells)

| windows | kappa | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe | Fills |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 126 | 0.80 | 34.83% | 54.4% | 0.94 | 477 |
| 126 | 0.90 | 36.36% | 57.3% | 0.93 | 417 |
| 168 | 0.80 | 35.66% | 52.9% | 0.95 | 556 |
| 168 | 0.90 | 37.48% | 55.9% | 0.94 | 498 |
| 210 | 0.80 | 31.82% | 56.8% | 0.86 | 690 |
| 210 | 0.90 | 33.15% | 59.9% | 0.86 | 628 |
| 126/168/210 | 0.80 | 37.35% | 54.2% | 0.98 | 722 |
| **126/168/210** | **0.90** | **39.39%** | **57.1%** | **0.97** | **686** |

Six of eight cells clear the published CAGR bar. The 210-session corner does
not (31.8-33.2%): a three-quarter-year window is too slow for the 2022 regime
change. The multi-window average is the robust choice and is the primary cell.

## Placebo and static attribution

* **Circular-shift placebo (100 shifts):** median CAGR 23.2%, 5th-95th range
  14.2-55.3%; the real 39.39% is at the **88th percentile**, below the 90%
  kill. Median placebo Sharpe 0.66 vs the real 0.97; the Sharpe percentile is
  90%.
* **Static book at the average weights (14.8/64.9/20.3):** 30.45% CAGR / 67.1%
  DD / 0.81 Sharpe. The Kelly timing adds 8.9 pp of CAGR and 0.16 Sharpe, so
  it is not a pure static mix, but the improvement is smaller than for beta or
  decay.

The wide placebo upper tail is the honest problem: some rotations of the same
allocation path land the high-TQQQ book on 2020-2021 and compound faster than
the real path. The Kelly state is informative on average, but not sharply
separated from a lucky rotation at the 90% confidence level.

## Correlation to the nine current winners

Range **0.47 to 0.89**. Highest: `relative-value-tqqq` 0.89, `ratio-froth`
0.79, `family-rebalance-flow` 0.79. This is the most correlated of the four new
families, as expected for a high-TQQQ-weight sizer. It is below the 0.95
duplicate threshold.

## Kill criteria

| Criterion | Result | Pass? |
|---|---|---|
| 1 bp CAGR > 36.72% | 39.39% | yes |
| 1 bp DD < 82.29% | 57.08% | yes |
| 10 bp CAGR > 36.72% | 37.61% | yes |
| Placebo percentile >= 90% | 88% | **no** |
| Max winner correlation <= 0.95 | 0.89 | yes |
| >= 100 fills / >= 30 events | 686 / 329 | yes |
| No negative subperiod | all positive | yes |
| Static blend not within 1 pp | 30.45% vs 39.39% | yes |

## Assessment

This is a real, active, reproducible strategy with a genuine numeric pass, but
it is **not a clean accept under its own pre-registered rule**. The failure is
specifically the placebo confidence test, not the return, drawdown, cost,
activity or duplication tests. Two honest options for the lead:

1. Accept it as a numeric above-TQQQ family with an explicit "weak timing"
   note; the static-blend and 10 bp results support a real sizing contribution.
2. Keep it as a research record and use `family-beta-rotation` and
   `family-tqqq-decay` as the two accepted families.

The report deliberately does not relax the 90% threshold after seeing 88%.

## Caveats

* The Kelly fraction is estimated on a rolling empirical sample; it is not a
  forecast of future mean or variance. In a regime change the estimate is
  stale for up to the window length.
* The fourth-order expansion is a local approximation; the 201-point grid and
  the `f in [0,1]` cap keep it bounded, but it is not an exact empirical Kelly
  optimiser.
* 2018 (-13.9%) and 2022 (-39.4%) are large losses. The family is not
  crash-protected.
* Transaction costs are modest because the 2% band suppresses small rebalances,
  but turnover is 450x and the 10 bp case gives up 1.8 pp of CAGR.

## Reproduce

```bash
cd research/new/family-kelly-sizing
python strategy.py        # rewrites result.json
```

`build_weights(ts, opens, closes)` accepts the shared minute panel or a daily
panel; the lead's `run_holdout.py` can call it directly.
hypothesis_md:
# family-kelly-sizing — hypothesis and pre-registration

**Slug:** `family-kelly-sizing`
**Family:** Kelly sizing
**Development window:** 2016-01-04 .. 2023-12-29 only. 2024-2026 is not loaded
or inspected.
**Benchmark bar:** TQQQ 36.72% CAGR / 82.29% max DD / 0.82 Sharpe (published
1-minute-mark bar). TQQQ on this panel is 35.81% / 82.30% / 0.80.

## 1. Mechanism

A fixed volatility target sizes the book by risk, not by edge. Kelly sizing
sizes it by the estimated growth rate of the bet:

```
f* = argmax_f E[log(1 + f * x)]
```

where `x` is the excess return of the TQQQ-over-QQQ overlay. For a Gaussian,
`f* = mean(x) / var(x)`. The strategy uses a fourth-order expansion of the log
growth on the empirical sample,

```
g(f) = f*mu - 0.5*f^2*var + (1/3)*f^3*m3 - 0.25*f^4*m4
```

so negative skew (`m3 < 0`) and fat tails (`m4`) reduce the Kelly fraction
relative to the Gaussian ratio. This is the sense in which the sizing uses
mean, variance **and skew**, rather than a pure vol target.

Two edges are estimated:

* `f_q = mean(r_QQQ) / var(r_QQQ)` — QQQ versus cash. If `f_q <= 0`, the
  unlevered index itself has no estimated edge and the book goes to BIL.
* `f_lev` — the Kelly fraction of `r_TQQQ - r_QQQ`, i.e. of the decision to
  replace a QQQ dollar with a TQQQ dollar. This is the leverage-sizing
  decision, not a separate asset-selection model.

The TQQQ weight is `clip(kappa * f_lev, 0, 1)`; QQQ takes the remainder. The
fractional cap is `kappa = 0.90` and the hard TQQQ weight cap is 100% of
capital.

## 2. Exact rules

All inputs use daily closes through session `t`; the target is set at that
close and executed at the first bar open of `t+1`.

1. Simple daily returns `r_Q,t = QQQ_t/QQQ_{t-1} - 1`, `r_T,t` likewise.
2. For each lookback `w in {126, 168, 210}`:
   * `f_q,w = mean(r_Q, w) / var(r_Q, w)`;
   * `f_lev,w = argmax_{f in [0,1]} g_w(f)` on the overlay `r_T - r_Q`, using
     201 equally spaced grid points and the four central moments of the
     window.
3. Average the available estimates: `f_q = mean_w f_q,w`,
   `f_lev = mean_w f_lev,w`. A window contributes only after it is full.
4. If `f_q <= 0` or no window is available: **BIL**.
   Otherwise `w_T = clip(0.90 * f_lev, 0, 1)`, `w_Q = 1 - w_T`, `w_BIL = 0`.
5. The target is held through the next session. Long-only, sum to 1.

## 3. Estimation window and decision clock

| Item | Choice |
|---|---|
| Kelly windows | 126, 168, 210 sessions, averaged |
| Overlay | `TQQQ simple return - QQQ simple return` |
| Expansion | fourth-order log-growth, `f in [0,1]`, 201 grid points |
| Fractional cap | 0.90 |
| Data | local adjusted 1-minute QQQ/TQQQ/BIL panel via `research/bt.py` |
| Decision | close of session `t` |
| Fill | first bar open of `t+1` |
| Costs | 1 bp headline; 5 bp and 10 bp reported |
| Band | 2% notional |

## 4. Why this is not an existing family

* Not a volatility target: the position is the estimated Kelly fraction of the
  leverage overlay, including its skew and kurtosis; there is no
  `target_vol / realised_vol` term.
* Not `relative-value-tqqq` or `ratio-froth`: no TQQQ/QQQ price ratio, no ratio
  momentum, no trend gate.
* Not `vol-scaled-crash-stop`: no drawdown or capitulation event.
* The name `vol-kelly-overlay-v2` in the archive is a different, retired
  volatility-spike reflation strategy; its own documentation says it does not
  use Kelly sizing. This family is the actual Kelly allocator.

## 5. Pre-registered 8-cell grid

| # | windows | kappa |
|---:|---|---:|
| 1 | 126 | 0.80 |
| 2 | 126 | 0.90 |
| 3 | 168 | 0.80 |
| 4 | 168 | 0.90 |
| 5 | 210 | 0.80 |
| 6 | 210 | 0.90 |
| 7 | 126, 168, 210 | 0.80 |
| 8 | **126, 168, 210** | **0.90** (primary) |

The primary is the multi-window average at 90% fractional Kelly. The single
windows are the robustness probes; the 210-session corner is expected to be the
weakest because it adapts slowest to a regime change.

## 6. Falsifiers (pre-registered)

1. 1 bp CAGR <= 36.72% or max DD >= 82.29%.
2. 10 bp CAGR <= 36.72%.
3. Circular-shift placebo CAGR percentile < 90%.
4. Correlation with any current winner > 0.95.
5. Fewer than 100 fills or fewer than 30 independent fill events.
6. Any subperiod with negative CAGR.
7. Static average-weight book within 1 pp of the 1 bp CAGR.

## 7. Expected effect

| metric | expectation |
|---|---|
| CAGR (1 bp) | 37-42% |
| max DD | 52-62% |
| Sharpe | 0.92-1.00 |
| average TQQQ weight | 0.55-0.70 |
| correlation to winners | 0.75-0.90 |

Kelly is an aggressive sizer: it will hold a high TQQQ weight in strong trends
and cut hard when the overlay's mean, variance or skew deteriorate. The
pre-registered placebo threshold is the main risk to acceptance; a high raw
CAGR with a placebo percentile below 90% means the sizing is mostly a
high-TQQQ beta, not a timing edge.

code:
"""family-kelly-sizing -- fractional Kelly sizing of the TQQQ/QQQ decision.

Primary object: the rolling Kelly fraction.  Two edges are estimated from daily
returns:

* ``f_q``   = mean(r_QQQ) / var(r_QQQ)          -- QQQ versus cash;
* ``f_lev`` = argmax_f E[log(1 + f (r_TQQQ - r_QQQ))] -- the TQQQ-over-QQQ
  overlay, evaluated with a fourth-order expansion of the log growth:

      g(f) = f*mu - 0.5*f^2*var + (1/3)*f^3*m3 - 0.25*f^4*m4

  so negative skew and fat tails reduce the Kelly fraction relative to the
  Gaussian ``mu/var``.  The leverage weight is ``clip(kappa * f_lev, 0, 1)``;
  QQQ takes the rest.  If ``f_q <= 0`` the QQQ edge itself is negative and the
  book goes to BIL.

The headline averages the 126/168/210-session estimates and uses
``kappa = 0.9``.  This is fractional Kelly with a hard 100% TQQQ cap.

Decision clock: moments use closes through session t; the target is executed at
the first bar open of t+1.

Run ``python strategy.py`` from this directory to regenerate ``result.json``.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

import harness

SLUG = "family-kelly-sizing"
FAMILY = "kelly-sizing"
PRIMARY = ("rolling Kelly fraction from QQQ/TQQQ mean, variance, skew and "
           "kurtosis (fourth-order log-growth expansion)")

PARAMS = {
    "windows": (126, 168, 210),
    "kappa": 0.90,
    "tqqq_cap": 1.00,
    "grid_points": 201,
}

PLATEAU = [
    {"windows": (126,), "kappa": 0.80},
    {"windows": (126,), "kappa": 0.90},
    {"windows": (168,), "kappa": 0.80},
    {"windows": (168,), "kappa": 0.90},
    {"windows": (210,), "kappa": 0.80},
    {"windows": (210,), "kappa": 0.90},
    {"windows": (126, 168, 210), "kappa": 0.80},
    {"windows": (126, 168, 210), "kappa": 0.90},
]


def _moments(returns: np.ndarray):
    mu = float(returns.mean())
    d = returns - mu
    var = float((d * d).mean())
    m3 = float((d ** 3).mean())
    m4 = float((d ** 4).mean())
    return mu, var, m3, m4


def _overlay_kelly(ex: np.ndarray, grid: np.ndarray) -> float:
    """Fourth-order log-growth Kelly fraction on [0, 1]."""
    mu, var, m3, m4 = _moments(ex)
    g = (grid * mu - 0.5 * (grid ** 2) * var
         + (1.0 / 3.0) * (grid ** 3) * m3
         - 0.25 * (grid ** 4) * m4)
    return float(grid[int(np.argmax(g))])


def make_targets(dates, closes: np.ndarray, params: dict | None = None) -> np.ndarray:
    p = dict(PARAMS)
    if params:
        p.update(params)
    nd = len(dates)
    rets = np.diff(closes, axis=0) / closes[:-1]      # simple returns
    grid = np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, int(p["grid_points"]))
    acc_q = np.zeros(nd)
    acc_l = np.zeros(nd)
    cnt = np.zeros(nd)
    for win in p["windows"]:
        win = int(win)
        for i in range(win, nd):
            x = rets[i - win:i]
            rq = x[:, 0]
            rt = x[:, 1]
            mu_q, var_q, _, _ = _moments(rq)
            acc_q[i] += mu_q / var_q if var_q > 0 else -1.0
            acc_l[i] += _overlay_kelly(rt - rq, grid)
            cnt[i] += 1
    f_q = np.divide(acc_q, np.maximum(cnt, 1))
    f_lev = np.divide(acc_l, np.maximum(cnt, 1))

    w = np.zeros((nd, 3))
    w[:, 2] = 1.0
    valid = (cnt > 0) & (f_q > 0.0)
    wt = np.clip(float(p["kappa"]) * f_lev[valid], 0.0, float(p["tqqq_cap"]))
    w[valid, 1] = wt
    w[valid, 0] = 1.0 - wt
    w[valid, 2] = 0.0
    return w


def build_weights(ts, o, c, params: dict | None = None) -> np.ndarray:
    dates, closes = harness.daily_closes(ts, c)
    daily = make_targets(dates, closes, params)
    if len(ts) == len(dates):
        return daily
    return harness.expand(ts, daily)


def _plateau(ts, o, c, dates, closes) -> list[dict]:
    out = []
    for cell in PLATEAU:
        w = harness.expand(ts, make_targets(dates, closes, cell))
        st = harness.metrics(harness.simulate(ts, o, c, w, bp=1.0))
        out.append({
            "cell": {"windows": list(cell["windows"]), "kappa": cell["kappa"]},
            "cagr": st["cagr"], "max_drawdown": st["max_drawdown"],
            "sharpe": st["sharpe"], "fills": st["fills"],
            "turnover": st["turnover"],
        })
    return out


def main() -> None:
    ts, o, c = harness.load_panel()
    dates, closes = harness.daily_closes(ts, c)
    daily = make_targets(dates, closes)
    ev = harness.evaluate(ts, o, c, daily, n_placebo=100)
    st = ev["stats"]["1bp"]
    max_corr = max(ev["corr_winners"].values())
    kills = {
        "cagr_below_published_tqqq_bar": st["cagr"] <= 0.3672,
        "drawdown_above_tqqq": st["max_drawdown"] >= 0.8229,
        "cost_10bp_below_bar": ev["stats"]["10bp"]["cagr"] <= 0.3672,
        "placebo_below_90pct": ev["placebo"]["cagr_percentile_of_real"] < 0.90,
        "correlation_above_0.95": max_corr > 0.95,
        "fewer_than_100_fills": st["fills"] < 100,
        "fewer_than_30_events": ev["events"] < 30,
        "negative_subperiod": any(v["cagr"] < 0 for v in ev["subperiods"].values()),
        "static_blend_matches": (ev["static_avg_weights"]["cagr"] >= st["cagr"] - 0.01),
    }
    verdict = "dev_pass" if not any(kills.values()) else "fail"
    payload = {
        "slug": SLUG, "family": FAMILY, "primary_object": PRIMARY,
        "dev": ev["stats"]["1bp"],
        "windows": {"dev": {"1bp": ev["stats"]["1bp"],
                            "5bp": ev["stats"]["5bp"],
                            "10bp": ev["stats"]["10bp"]}},
        "window": {"dev": [harness.START, harness.END], "holdout": "not loaded"},
        "benchmark": {
            "tqqq_panel": {"cagr": 0.3581, "max_drawdown": 0.823, "sharpe": 0.80},
            "tqqq_published_bar": {"cagr": 0.3672, "max_drawdown": 0.8229,
                                   "sharpe": 0.82},
        },
        "params": {k: (list(v) if isinstance(v, tuple) else v)
                   for k, v in PARAMS.items()},
        "stats": ev["stats"], "events": ev["events"],
        "yearly": ev["yearly"], "subperiods": ev["subperiods"],
        "corr_winners": ev["corr_winners"],
        "corr_range": [min(ev["corr_winners"].values()),
                       max(ev["corr_winners"].values())],
        "avg_weights": ev["avg_weights"],
        "static_avg_weights": ev["static_avg_weights"],
        "plateau": _plateau(ts, o, c, dates, closes),
        "placebo": ev["placebo"],
        "kill_checks": kills, "verdict": verdict,
        "timing": ("Moments use daily simple returns through session t; target "
                   "executed at the first bar open of t+1; 2% band."),
        "notes": ("The Kelly fraction is the maximiser of a fourth-order "
                  "log-growth expansion on the empirical overlay sample, so "
                  "skew and kurtosis enter explicitly. Fractional cap 0.9 and "
                  "a hard 100% TQQQ weight cap. No 2024-2026 rows are read."),
    }
    harness.write_result(Path(__file__).with_name("result.json"), payload)
    print(f"{SLUG}: {harness.summary_line(st)}")
    print("  10bp:", harness.summary_line(ev["stats"]["10bp"]))
    print("  corr range", payload["corr_range"], "verdict", verdict)
    print("  kills", [k for k, v in kills.items() if v])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
